content: I'll start by reading the test image, then systematically check one reference image per class.

**Test image analysis:** The leaf shows a prominent cream/white stripe running along the midrib, with the surrounding blade remaining green. There are a few small reddish spots scattered on the leaf surface. The midrib yellowing/paling is the dominant feature.

Now I'll check one reference per class. Starting with Yellow_Leaf (most likely given midrib discoloration).
Yellow_Leaf reference shows yellowing/browning leaves radiating from center, but with yellowing of the midrib stripe visible. Now checking Brown_Spot.
Brown_Spot reference shows reddish-brown oval lesions on leaf — the reddish spots in the test image are smaller/less prominent. Now checking Grassy_Shoot.
Grassy_Shoot shows many thin grass-like shoots with pale midrib stripes — similar midrib coloring to the test image. Now checking Pokkah_Boeng for my final reference view.

**Pokkah_Boeng reference** shows a stem with a twisted/deformed leaf at the node ("knife cut" symptom) — very different from the test image.

**Synthesis of all evidence:**

| Feature | Test Image | Match |
|---|---|---|
| Cream/white midrib stripe | Prominent, runs full length | Yellow_Leaf ✓ (midrib yellowing is hallmark) |
| Green leaf blade | Both sides of midrib are green | Yellow_Leaf ✓ |
| Small reddish spots | A few scattered | Brown_Spot (partial) |
| Leaf morphology | Normal single sugarcane leaf | Not Grassy_Shoot (which shows thin grassy proliferation) |
| Distortion/deformation | None | Rules out Pokkah_Boeng |

The dominant symptom is the **bright cream/white midrib stripe** with green blade on both sides — this is the classic presentation of **Yellow Leaf disease** (SCYLV), where the virus specifically discolors the midrib while the blade stays green. The small reddish spots are minor secondary features and insufficient to reclassify as Brown_Spot. The single normal-sized leaf rules out Grassy_Shoot, and no deformation rules out Pokkah_Boeng.
